rationale: Engineering leads at small AI-heavy dev teams (2–20 people) are demonstrably paying $500–$1,000+/month in cloud AI subscriptions and actively looking for cost relief — willingness to pay is real and evidenced by current spend, not speculation. The service (a cloud-vs-local LLM cost analysis report + threshold monitor delivered as a recurring automated report) can be built as a Claude-powered intake form + calculation engine + Stripe subscription with near-zero per-customer manual work. The main risk is that this niche is small enough that lead volume may be limited, and no responsiveness data exists yet — validate the channel (LinkedIn/HN outreach to eng leads) before scaling.
solution_plan: The micro-service is an AI Cost Routing Advisor: a monthly automated report that tells a dev team exactly which of their Claude/OpenAI workloads would be cheaper on local models (Apple Silicon, etc.) and what hardware ROI looks like at their spend level. The factory builds it as a Claude prompt pipeline that ingests a team's spend data (via a simple intake form), runs cost/ROI math, and emails a plain-English PDF report — no coding by Youval. To sell it, the factory drafts LinkedIn and HN outreach messages targeting engineering leads and CTOs at software shops who post about AI costs; Youval approves each outreach batch before it goes out. After signup via Stripe ($49–$99/month), delivery is fully automated: monthly spend form reminder → Claude analysis → PDF report → email delivery, all handled by the factory. The only recurring human touch is approving the monthly outreach batch and reviewing any edge-case support tickets flagged by Claude.
